title: Exploring content of misinformation about HPV vaccine on twitter
screen_reason: Retrospective content analysis of a #HPV Twitter keyword corpus in which every tweet was human-coded as containing disinformation/misinformation or as supportive/educational, and the share of the corpus that was misinformation is reported with its denominator (931/3,876 = 24.0%). This is a CONTENT estimate: the denominator is all items retrieved by the hashtag search.

estimates.country: Not stated; English-language Twitter stream (authors US-based)
estimates.measure_type: % of #HPV tweets coded as containing disinformation/misinformation about the HPV vaccine
estimates.denominator: 3,876 unique English-language #HPV tweets (retweets excluded) retained after data cleaning, posted by 1,780 unique users
estimates.definition: A tweet was counted in the numerator if annotators coded it as raising a concern about the HPV vaccine containing disinformation/misinformation; concern subcategories were health, other safety, big pharma, government, mandatory, ineffective, vague/general, other, and common concerns in the literature. Tweets that raised no concern were coded support/education.
estimates.misinfo_def: "information, defined as the inadvertent spread of false or incomplete beliefs without intent to cause harm" (misinformation); disinformation is "content that has been created and shared with intentional deception"
estimates.page_loc: p. 244, Table 1 (Number (Percent) of support versus misinformation #HPV tweets by study month); same figure stated in the Abstract and in Results, 'Frequency of misinformation'
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Four trained annotators coded each tweet in REDCap against an iteratively developed codebook; a fifth reviewer (MLK) crosschecked the dichotomous coding and computed Fleiss kappa = 0.91 across the four annotators on a 152-tweet reliability set.

estimates.notes: Single-issue hashtag corpus (#HPV), so denom_scope=topical; a random 80% (4,258 of 5,341 retrieved tweets) was annotated, which is random subsampling rather than curation, so denom_selection is left empty. Judgement calls: (a) the 931 'misinformation' tweets include 16 tweets (2%) coded as 'concerns in the literature' (child too young, no provider recommendation, not required by school), which are legitimate concerns rather than false claims, and include the 'mandatory vaccination' (n=180) and 'vague/general' (n=64) categories, so the numerator is broader than factual falsity — coded breadth=misleading; (b) year set to 2020 because three of the three-and-a-half collection months fall in 2020; (c) the paper reports 4,824 coded posts in Data cleaning but 4,258 tweets selected for annotation in Search strategy, an internal inconsistency that does not affect the final 3,876 denominator.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (1) the misinformation subcategory shares (health 539/931 = 58%, mandatory 180/931 = 19%, ineffective 127/931 = 14%, other safety 106 (11%), government 69 (8%), big pharma 65 (8%), vague 64 (8%), other 40 (5%), literature concerns 16 (2%), Table 3) and the health-subcategory shares (harm NOS 51%, death 23%, cancer 17%, Fig. 1) — these are the topical composition of a misinformation-only set, not a share of items judged false, and the categories are explicitly not mutually exclusive; (2) the monthly rows of Table 1 (Dec 15–31 2019 35.7%, Jan 21.8%, Feb 23.2%, Mar 25.1%) — collapsed to the Total row as the representative point per the time-series rule; (3) '60% (n = 1758)' of supportive posts mentioning the HPV vaccine, which is a share of true content, not misinformation; (4) engagement statistics (mean retweets, IRRs such as 5.44) are ratios and counts, not shares with a misinformation denominator; (5) the '41% of parents have been exposed to disinformation and/or misinformation' figure in the Introduction is cited from Gunaratne et al. and is therefore excluded under R8.

rob.design: Retrospective content analysis of the Twitter API stream, 15 Dec 2019 – 31 Mar 2020, English-language filter, retweets excluded, hashtag '#HPV'; 5,342 tweets retrieved, 1 non-English removed, a random 80% (4,258) selected for manual annotation; codebook developed iteratively over 25 then 53 then 152 development tweets; four annotators coded independently in REDCap, Fleiss kappa 0.91 on the 152-tweet reliability set, crosschecked by a fifth reviewer; 699 posts containing neither support nor concern and 249 user-text-date duplicates were dropped, leaving 3,876 posts by 1,780 unique users (3,710 unique text posts). No response rate applies (platform data). Coding of intent was explicitly not attempted; all disinformation/misinformation posts were pooled as 'misinformation'.
